doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Discovering the Hammond organ in the Army
summary: Levin found a Hammond organ at his Army band hall in the late 60s, began playing R&B groups, and still loves the instrument.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Your tastes seem to be pretty wide ranging. I’m curious how this Hammond organ thing came about.

Oh I was in the Army in the late 60s, and I had been playing jazz piano in school just on the side. And I got into the Army and I was looking for ways to play. And there was a Hammond organ at the unit — well it was at the band rehearsal hall where I was stationed. And somebody else had been using it and he cranked it up for me once and showed me how it worked, and I says oh this is pretty nice. I started playing with R&B groups after that, playing organ. It’s a great instrument. It’s got this sound, it’s like a human voice I think, just the aesthetics of it. It obviously isn’t, it’s electronic, but it just has that vibe to it. It’s still my favorite keyboard instrument. It’s the one that does the most for me here. It’s a long term on it, I’ve owned a lot of keyboard instruments, I still do, now I just get them in modules, you know like the six foot racks of synths. But I went through a long period of my favorite bands were the ones where they would let me play organ. And now it’s a resurgence. It’s great. It’s back. Now everybody wants you to do it. And my problem is moving my Hammond, which I can’t lift it anymore.
